question: How do you implement efficient batch embedding for millions of documents?
diagram:
[10M docs] -> [Chunker] -> [Batch: 1000 chunks/request] -> [Parallel workers] -> [Async upsert to vector DB]
Monitor: throughput, failures, cost
hinglish_explanation: Millions documents embed karne ke liye batch processing chahiye - sequential nahi chalega. Parallel workers, batch API (OpenAI batch 50% cheaper), async upsert, checkpointing for failures, progress monitoring. 10M docs = 2-3 days typical with proper pipeline.
real_life_example: Amazon warehouse mein lakho items sort karna - ek-ek nahi, conveyor belt pe batch mein. Same with embeddings - 1000 chunks per batch, parallel workers, assembly line approach.
how_to_answer:
- Batch size: 1000-2000 chunks per API call
- Parallel workers: 10-50 concurrent embedding requests
- OpenAI Batch API: 50% cheaper, 24hr turnaround
- Checkpointing: resume from last successful batch on failure
- Rate limiting: respect API limits with backoff
- Cost estimate: 10M chunks x 500 tokens = ~$100 (text-embedding-3-small)
- Pipeline: chunk -> queue -> embed workers -> upsert workers
- I use async Python + Redis queue for large ingestion jobs

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'agentic RAG' and how does it differ from standard RAG?
diagram:
Standard RAG: fixed retrieve-then-generate
Agentic RAG: agent decides when/what/how to retrieve, can iterate, use tools
hinglish_explanation: Agentic RAG matlab retrieval ko agent ke decision making mein integrate karna - agent decide kare kab retrieve, kya retrieve, kitni baar, kaunsa source. Iterative, adaptive, tool-using. Standard RAG fixed pipeline hai, agentic RAG intelligent orchestration.
real_life_example: Standard RAG = vending machine (button dabao, item aaye). Agentic RAG = personal shopper (tumhari need samjhe, multiple stores check kare, best option laaye). Smarter but complex.
how_to_answer:
- Agent controls retrieval decisions dynamically
- Can: retrieve multiple times, from different sources, refine queries
- Decides: when to retrieve, whether to retrieve at all
- Iterates until answer quality is sufficient
- Tools: web search, SQL, calculators alongside retrieval
- Implementation: LangGraph with retrieval as a tool
- More powerful for complex queries, higher latency/cost
- I build agentic RAG for complex enterprise QA

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you implement and optimize RAG for edge devices (mobile/IoT)?
diagram:
[Small embedding model (384d)] + [Quantized on-device LLM] + [Local vector store]
Constraints: 2GB RAM, no internet, low latency
hinglish_explanation: Edge RAG mein extreme constraints hain - limited RAM, no internet, battery. Small models (MiniLM-384d), quantized LLMs (Phi-3-mini Q4), local vector store (SQLite + HNSW). Preprocessing on server, inference on device. Privacy-first use cases demand this.
real_life_example: Offline dictionary app jaisa - internet nahi but search kaam kare. Medical worker rural area mein - offline RAG on tablet for patient guidelines. Privacy + connectivity constraints drive edge RAG.
how_to_answer:
- Small embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d, 80MB)
- Quantized LLM: Phi-3-mini Q4, Gemma-2B Q4
- Local vector store: SQLite-VSS, Faiss flat index
- Pre-process and pre-embed on server, sync to device
- Limit corpus size (10k-100k chunks max)
- Optimize: reduce dimensions, PQ compression
- Use cases: offline medical guides, field service, privacy
- Trade-off: quality vs size/speed constraints

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the purpose of overlap in text chunking?
diagram:
[Chunk 1: tokens 1-500] [Overlap: tokens 450-500] [Chunk 2: tokens 450-950]
Overlap preserves context at boundaries
hinglish_explanation: Overlap matlab chunks ke boundaries pe kuch text dono chunks mein hota hai. Bina overlap, sentence beech mein kat jaata hai aur context lose hota hai. 10-20% overlap standard hai. Too much overlap = redundancy aur storage waste.
real_life_example: Book ke chapters mein last paragraph next chapter ki intro mein bhi refer hota hai - context continuity. Chunk overlap same - boundary pe information loss prevent karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Shared text between consecutive chunks at boundaries
- Prevents information loss when sentences span chunk boundary
- Typical: 10-20% of chunk size (50-100 tokens for 500-token chunk)
- Too little: broken context at boundaries
- Too much: redundancy, storage waste, duplicate retrievals
- Some chunkers overlap by sentence count instead of tokens
- Critical for: long sentences, flowing narratives
- I use 50-100 token overlap with recursive splitter

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between retrieval augmentation and tool augmentation?
diagram:
Retrieval: fetch text knowledge -> add to context
Tool: execute action (calculator, API, DB query) -> add result to context
hinglish_explanation: Retrieval augmentation text fetch karta hai (documents), tool augmentation actions execute karta hai (calculate, API call, DB query). Dono LLM ko external info dete hain but nature different hai. Modern agents dono use karte hain.
real_life_example: Retrieval = library se book laana (passive information). Tool = lab mein experiment karna (active action). Dono answers dete hain but method different.
how_to_answer:
- Retrieval: passive, fetches existing text/knowledge
- Tool: active, executes actions and returns results
- Retrieval: documents, KB articles, web pages
- Tools: calculators, APIs, database queries, code execution
- Modern agents combine both
- RAG = retrieval augmentation specifically
- Function calling enables tool augmentation
- I design systems with both retrieval and tool access

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you measure the cost-effectiveness of a RAG system?
diagram:
Cost per query = (embedding cost + retrieval cost + LLM cost) / total queries
ROI = (manual support cost saved - RAG system cost) / RAG system cost
hinglish_explanation: RAG cost-effectiveness measure karna hai to: per-query cost (embedding + search + LLM), total monthly cost, vs alternative (human support cost). ROI positive hona chahiye. Optimization: caching, smaller models, token reduction.
real_life_example: Call center agent $10/hour, 20 queries/hour = $0.50/query. RAG bot $0.05/query. 10x cheaper - but quality comparable honi chahiye. Cost + quality dono measure karo.
how_to_answer:
- Per-query cost: embedding + vector search + LLM tokens
- Typical: $0.01-0.10 per RAG query (GPT-4o-mini + Pinecone)
- Compare to: human agent cost per resolution
- Track: monthly cost, cost per successful resolution
- Optimize: caching (30-70% reduction), smaller models, less tokens
- ROI calculation: savings vs build + maintain cost
- Break-even: typically 2-3 months at scale
- I track cost/query and optimize weekly

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between open-book and closed-book QA?
diagram:
Closed-book: LLM answers from memory (training data only)
Open-book: LLM answers with external context (RAG, retrieval)
hinglish_explanation: Closed-book matlab LLM sirf apni training memory se answer de - hallucination risk high. Open-book matlab external documents provide karo (RAG). Open-book = exam mein books allowed, closed-book = pure memory se. RAG is open-book QA.
real_life_example: Board exam (closed-book) vs open-book test. Open-book mein reference material use kar sakte ho - accuracy better, cheating kam. RAG LLM ko open-book exam de raha hai basically.
how_to_answer:
- Closed-book: model relies only on parametric knowledge (training)
- Open-book: model has access to external documents/context
- RAG is essentially open-book QA
- Closed-book issues: hallucination, knowledge cutoff, no citations
- Open-book benefits: grounded, verifiable, up-to-date
- Closed-book still useful for: common knowledge, reasoning
- Hybrid: try closed-book first, RAG if uncertain
- Modern approach: RAG for facts, model knowledge for reasoning

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the role of a query classifier in RAG systems?
diagram:
[Query] -> [Classifier] -> {factual | analytical | conversational | out-of-scope}
Each type -> different handling strategy
hinglish_explanation: Query classifier pehle query ka type identify karta hai - factual (RAG), analytical (multi-step), conversational (memory), out-of-scope (reject). Different types ko different strategies se handle karna optimal hai. Simple LLM classifier ya fine-tuned small model use karo.
real_life_example: Hospital reception - emergency? Direct ER. Regular checkup? OPD. Lab test? Lab counter. Query classifier same triage karta hai - right handling for right query type.
how_to_answer:
- Classify query type before processing
- Types: factual, analytical, conversational, out-of-scope, greeting
- Each type gets different pipeline/strategy
- Implementation: LLM with classification prompt, or fine-tuned classifier
- Factual -> RAG, Analytical -> decompose + RAG, Greeting -> direct response
- Saves cost: not every query needs retrieval
- Improves UX: appropriate response for each type
- I implement as first step in every production RAG

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between extractive summarization and abstractive summarization?
diagram:
Extractive: pick important sentences from source (no new words)
Abstractive: generate new summary in own words (can paraphrase)
hinglish_explanation: Extractive summarization source se important sentences select karta hai - copy-paste type. Abstractive apne words mein naya summary generate karta hai - LLMs yeh karte hain. Abstractive more natural but hallucination risk. RAG mein abstractive common hai.
real_life_example: News article ka first paragraph as summary = extractive. Apne words mein 2 lines mein explain = abstractive. LLMs abstractive mein expert hain but facts verify karna important.
how_to_answer:
- Extractive: selects key sentences from source verbatim
- Abstractive: generates new text capturing main ideas
- LLMs excel at abstractive summarization
- Extractive: 100% faithful, less fluent
- Abstractive: more natural, can hallucinate details
- Use in RAG: summarize retrieved docs before passing to LLM
- Or: summarize long documents for indexing
- Map-reduce summarization for very long docs

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the importance of error handling in LLM applications?
diagram:
Errors: API timeout, rate limit, invalid output, hallucination, context overflow
Handling: retry, fallback, validation, graceful degradation
hinglish_explanation: LLM apps mein multiple failure points hain - API down, rate limit, malformed output, context overflow. Production mein har failure gracefully handle hona chahiye. User ko never crash dikhna chahiye - fallback, retry, cached response, or polite error message.
real_life_example: ATM mein 'service unavailable' aata hai when bank server down - but ATM crash nahi hota. LLM app bhi same - API fail ho to graceful message, crash nahi.
how_to_answer:
- Common failures: API timeout, 429 rate limit, malformed JSON, hallucination
- Retry with exponential backoff for transient errors
- Fallback: cheaper model if primary fails
- Output validation: parse and verify before returning
- Circuit breaker: stop calling if error rate high
- Graceful degradation: cached response > error message > crash
- Logging: all errors with context for debugging
- I implement 3 retries + fallback model + cached response

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'grounding' in LLMs?
diagram:
Grounding: connecting LLM output to verifiable facts/sources
Ungrounded: LLM makes up plausible-sounding claims
hinglish_explanation: Grounding matlab LLM ka output verifiable sources se connected hona - citations, retrieved documents, tool outputs. Ungrounded = hallucination risk. RAG is a grounding technique. Google's Gemini API has explicit grounding features.
real_life_example: News anchor facts ke saath source cite karta hai - 'Reuters ke according...' (grounded). Rumor spread karna without source (ungrounded). LLM grounding = har claim ka source hona.
how_to_answer:
- Connecting LLM output to verifiable external data
- RAG is primary grounding technique
- Google grounding: Gemini API with Google Search grounding
- Methods: retrieval, citations, tool verification
- Ungrounded = high hallucination risk
- Grounded responses include: source, date, confidence
- Critical for: enterprise, healthcare, finance, legal
- I always implement grounding + citation in production

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between single-vector and multi-vector representations?
diagram:
Single-vector: one embedding per document (fast, simple)
Multi-vector: multiple embeddings per document (ColBERT, richer)
hinglish_explanation: Single-vector matlab ek document = ek embedding. Simple, fast search. Multi-vector matlab ek document ke multiple embeddings - token level (ColBERT) ya aspect level. More expressive but more storage and compute.
real_life_example: Passport photo (single vector) vs 10 different angle photos (multi-vector). Pehla quick identification, doosra more accurate recognition. Trade-off between speed and accuracy.
how_to_answer:
- Single-vector: one embedding per chunk (standard approach)
- Multi-vector: multiple embeddings per chunk (richer representation)
- ColBERT: token-level multi-vector
- Multi-aspect: separate embeddings for title, content, summary
- Single: fast retrieval, less storage
- Multi: better retrieval quality, more storage (10-128x)
- Choose based on: accuracy needs vs infrastructure budget
- I start single-vector, upgrade to multi if accuracy insufficient

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you implement user feedback collection for RAG improvement?
diagram: [Response] -> [Thumbs up/down] + [Optional comment] -> [Feedback DB] -> [Weekly analysis] -> [Fix] -> [Eval]
hinglish_explanation: User feedback sabse valuable signal hai RAG improve karne ke liye. Thumbs up/down, regeneration clicks, copy actions, time spent - sab implicit signals hain. Weekly analysis karke common failures fix karo. Feedback loop RAG quality continuously improve karta hai.
real_life_example: Uber/Ola ride ke baad rating dete ho - low ratings investigate hote hain, driver training hoti hai. RAG mein same - bad ratings analyze karke retrieval ya prompt fix karo.
how_to_answer:
- Collect: thumbs up/down, comments, regeneration, copy events
- Store: query, response, retrieved chunks, feedback, timestamp
- Analyze weekly: categorize failures, find patterns
- Root cause: retrieval issue vs generation issue
- Fix: add missing docs, improve chunking, adjust prompt
- Re-evaluate on fixed queries
- Build failed queries into golden dataset
- I maintain feedback dashboard with failure categorization

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How would you implement a production RAG system with automatic prompt optimization?
diagram:
[Eval results] -> [DSPy/OPRO optimizer] -> [Iterate prompts] -> [Select best performing] -> [Deploy]
Automatic rather than manual prompt tuning
hinglish_explanation: Automatic prompt optimization matlab manually prompt tune karne ki jagah algorithmic approach - DSPy, OPRO jaise tools automatically best prompt dhundhte hain based on eval metrics. Human creativity still needed for initial design, but optimization automated ho sakta hai.
real_life_example: Machine learning hyperparameter tuning jaisa - manually lr=0.001 try karna vs Optuna se automated search. Prompt optimization same concept - systematic search for best prompt.
how_to_answer:
- Tools: DSPy (Stanford), OPRO (Google), PromptBreeder
- DSPy: programs prompts as modules, optimizes with labeled data
- OPRO: LLM optimizes its own prompts iteratively
- Process: define metric -> provide examples -> auto-optimize
- Typical improvement: 10-30% over manual prompts
- Still needs: initial prompt design, good eval set
- Risk: overfitting to eval set
- I use DSPy for systematic prompt optimization in production

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'retrieval-aware training' and how does it improve RAG?
diagram:
Train LLM WITH retrieval context during training (not just inference)
Model learns: when to use context, when to ignore noise, how to cite
hinglish_explanation: Retrieval-aware training matlab LLM ko training time pe bhi retrieved documents dena - model seekhta hai kaise context use karna, noise ignore karna, cite karna. Standard LLMs sirf inference pe context dekhte hain - retrieval-aware models better handle karte hain noisy context.
real_life_example: Cricket player practice mein bhi match conditions simulate karta hai (crowd noise, pressure). Retrieval-aware training same - model practice mein bhi noisy context handle karna seekhta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Train LLM with retrieval during training, not just inference
- Model learns: use context, ignore noise, generate citations
- Examples: RETRO, Atlas, REALM, RAFT
- Better than: post-hoc RAG on standard LLM
- Handles noisy/irrelevant retrieved docs gracefully
- Reduces hallucination from incorrect context
- Currently: mostly research, some in production
- Practical alternative: RAFT (fine-tune with retrieval context)

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you implement observability for a RAG system in production?
diagram:
Monitor: retrieval latency, LLM latency, cache hit rate, error rate, faithfulness, cost/query
Tools: LangSmith, Datadog, custom dashboards
hinglish_explanation: RAG observability matlab har component ka health monitor karna - retrieval latency, LLM latency, cache hit ratio, error rate, answer quality metrics. Without observability, problems silently accumulate. LangSmith + custom dashboards standard approach hai.
real_life_example: Car dashboard - speed, fuel, temperature, engine light. Sab ek glance mein dikhe. RAG dashboard same - latency, quality, cost, errors ek jagah pe visible hone chahiye.
how_to_answer:
- Key metrics: retrieval latency, generation latency, total E2E
- Quality: faithfulness score (sampled), no-answer rate
- Cost: $/query, tokens/query, cache hit rate
- Errors: API failures, timeout rate, parse failures
- Traces: full request lifecycle (LangSmith, Langfuse)
- Alerts: latency spike, quality drop, cost anomaly
- Dashboard: real-time + daily/weekly trends
- I use LangSmith for traces + Grafana for metrics

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the 'hypothetical questions' indexing technique?
diagram:
[Document chunk] -> [LLM generates 3-5 questions this chunk answers] -> [Embed questions] -> [Store: question embedding -> chunk]
[User query] -> matches question embeddings (Q-Q similarity)
hinglish_explanation: Hypothetical questions technique matlab document chunks ke liye LLM se 3-5 questions generate karo jo us chunk se answer ho sakti hain. Questions embed karo. Search query aur generated questions compare hote hain - question-to-question similarity better hoti hai.
real_life_example: Teacher guide mein har chapter ke end mein possible questions diye hote hain. Student ka question in questions se match karo - chapter directly mil jaayega. Same concept RAG mein.
how_to_answer:
- LLM generates hypothetical questions for each chunk
- Index question embeddings (not chunk embeddings)
- At query time: compare user query to generated questions
- Q-Q similarity better than Q-Document similarity
- 3-5 questions per chunk typical
- Cost: one-time LLM calls during indexing
- Improves retrieval recall significantly
- I use this for FAQ-style knowledge bases

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How would you handle RAG for time-series or temporal data?
diagram:
[Time-series events] -> [Window-based chunking] -> [Temporal metadata] -> [Time-aware retrieval: recency + relevance]
[Query] -> filter by time range + semantic search
hinglish_explanation: Temporal data RAG mein time context matter karta hai - 'last month revenue' vs 'last year revenue' different results chahiye. Temporal metadata mandatory, time-range filters, recency-weighted scoring. Standard RAG time-agnostic hai - temporal awareness add karna padta hai.
real_life_example: Stock market data - 'RELIANCE stock performance' ka answer last week aur last year ke liye alag hoga. Temporal RAG time-aware retrieval karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Add temporal metadata: timestamp, valid_from, valid_to
- Time-range filtering before semantic search
- Recency-weighted scoring: newer docs rank higher
- Temporal chunking: group by time windows
- Handle: 'last month', 'Q3 2024', 'yesterday' (parse time expressions)
- Time-decay function for scoring
- Version control: which data was valid when
- I implement time-range filters + recency boost in retrieval

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between Langfuse and LangSmith?
diagram:
LangSmith: by LangChain, tight integration, experiments

hinglish_explanation: LangSmith LangChain ka official tool hai - tight integration but vendor lock-in. Langfuse open-source hai, self-host kar sakte ho, any framework ke saath kaam karta hai. real_life_example: LangSmith = Apple ecosystem (tight integration, closed). Langfuse = Android (open, flexible, self-host). Dono kaam karte hain, philosophy different hai.
how_to_answer:
- LangSmith: LangChain's official platform, best integration
- Langfuse: open-source, self-hostable, framework-agnostic
- Both provide: tracing, evaluation, datasets, monitoring
- LangSmith: easier if already using LangChain
- Langfuse: better for multi-framework, privacy (self-host)

- Cost: LangSmith free tier generous, Langfuse self-host = free

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the role of embedding fine-tuning for domain-specific RAG?
diagram: Generic embedding model -> fine-tune on domain (query, positive_doc, negative_doc) triples -> domain-adapted model
hinglish_explanation: Generic embeddings (OpenAI, BGE) general text pe trained hain. Tumhare domain (medical, legal, code) mein specific terminology hai - fine-tuning se embeddings domain-aware ban jaati hain. 10-30% retrieval improvement possible. Small labeled set (1000+ pairs) chahiye.
real_life_example: Generic translator vs medical translator - medical terms specialization chahiye. Embedding model ko bhi domain-specific fine-tune karne se retrieval accuracy significantly improve hoti hai.
how_to_answer:
- Fine-tune embedding model on domain-specific data
- Training data: (query, positive_doc, negative_doc) triples
- Minimum: 1000-5000 training triples
- Methods: contrastive learning, in-batch negatives
- Models: fine-tune sentence-transformers or BGE
- Typical improvement: 10-30% recall
- Tools: sentence-transformers library, synthetic data generation
- I fine-tune when off-the-shelf retrieval plateaus (<80% recall)

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you handle document deduplication in RAG?
diagram: [New doc] -> [MinHash/SimHash fingerprint] -> [Compare to existing] -> {exact dup: skip | near dup: merge/latest | unique: add}
hinglish_explanation: Duplicate documents RAG mein noise create karte hain - same info multiple times retrieve hoti hai, context waste hota hai. Exact dedup (hash) + near dedup (MinHash, SimHash) dono handle karne padtein hain. Ingestion pipeline mein dedup step must hai.
real_life_example: Email inbox mein same email 5 baar aaye to confusing. RAG index mein same document multiple versions ho to retrieval polluted hota hai. Dedup clean index maintain karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Exact dedup: content hash comparison (MD5, SHA256)
- Near dedup: MinHash, SimHash, embedding similarity
- Threshold: >0.95 similarity = probable duplicate
- Strategy: keep latest version, remove older
- Run at ingestion time (prevent duplicates entering)
- Periodic batch dedup for existing index
- Also dedup at retrieval time (diverse results)
- I implement MinHash dedup in ingestion pipeline

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'faithfulness' in RAG evaluation?
diagram:
Faithfulness = are ALL claims in the answer supported by retrieved context?
Faithful: every statement has evidence | Unfaithful: some claims made up
hinglish_explanation: Faithfulness matlab answer mein jo bhi claims hain, kya sab retrieved context se supported hain? Agar answer mein kuch aisa hai jo context mein nahi tha - that's hallucination/unfaithfulness. RAGAS ka most important metric hai. Production mein track karna must hai.
real_life_example: Court mein witness testimony - judge check karta hai 'kya evidence se match karta hai?' Jo match nahi woh inadmissible. Faithfulness same - answer mein sirf wahi hona chahiye jo context support karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Core RAG metric: claims in answer supported by context?
- Score: 0 (completely hallucinated) to 1 (fully faithful)
- Computation: extract claims from answer, check each against context
- RAGAS faithfulness metric automates this via LLM
- Most critical metric for production RAG
- Low faithfulness = hallucination problem
- Improvement: better prompt ('only use context'), citations
- Target: >0.85 faithfulness in production

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is prompt decomposition and when do you use it?
diagram:
Complex query: 'Compare A and B across X, Y, Z dimensions'
-> Decompose: [Get A-X, A-Y, A-Z, B-X, B-Y, B-Z] -> Synthesize
hinglish_explanation: Prompt decomposition matlab complex task ko simpler sub-tasks mein todna - har sub-task independently solve karo fir combine. Comparison questions, multi-part analysis, research queries ke liye use hota hai. Better accuracy than single complex prompt.
real_life_example: Board exam mein bada question parts mein hota hai - (a), (b), (c). Har part alag solve karo, fir combine. Complex RAG queries bhi same - decompose, solve parts, synthesize.
how_to_answer:
- Break complex query into simpler sub-queries
- Each sub-query: independent retrieval and generation
- Synthesize sub-answers into final response
- Use for: comparisons, multi-part analysis, research
- Tools: LlamaIndex SubQuestionQueryEngine
- Better accuracy than single complex prompt
- Trade-off: more LLM calls, higher latency
- I decompose queries with >2 distinct information needs

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you implement RAG with multi-modal inputs (voice, image, text queries)?
diagram:
[Voice] -> Whisper STT -> text query
[Image] -> GPT-4V description -> text query
[Text] -> direct
All -> unified RAG pipeline
hinglish_explanation: Multi-modal input RAG mein voice (Whisper se transcribe), image (Vision model se describe), text - sab ko unified text query mein convert karo fir standard RAG. Input normalization layer chahiye. Each modality ke liye preprocessing different.
real_life_example: Google Lens - photo lo, text search ho jaata hai. Voice assistant - bolo, text query ban jaata hai. Multi-modal RAG sab inputs handle karta hai - convert to text then process.
how_to_answer:
- Voice input: Whisper/Deepgram STT -> text query
- Image input: GPT-4V/Claude Vision -> text description -> query
- Unified text pipeline after conversion
- Handle: accent, image quality, ambiguity
- Latency: add transcription/vision time (200-1000ms)
- Fallback: 'could you rephrase?' on low-confidence transcription
- Multi-modal retrieval also possible (CLIP embeddings)
- I build input normalization layer for each modality

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'retrieval diversity' and why does it matter?
diagram:
Top-5 all from same section = low diversity (redundant)
Top-5 from different sections = high diversity (comprehensive)
MMR algorithm balances relevance + diversity
hinglish_explanation: Retrieval diversity matlab retrieved documents mein variety honi chahiye - sab same section se nahi. MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) algorithm relevance aur diversity balance karta hai. Without diversity, answer one-sided ho sakta hai especially for broad queries.
real_life_example: News padhte waqt - sirf ek newspaper se nahi, multiple sources se padhte ho balanced view ke liye. RAG retrieval bhi diverse honi chahiye - different angles cover hone chahiye.
how_to_answer:
- Problem: top-k docs may all cover same aspect (redundant)
- MMR: Maximal Marginal Relevance balances relevance + diversity
- Formula: argmax[lambda * sim(q,d) - (1-lambda) * max(sim(d,d_selected))]
- Lambda: 0.5-0.7 typical (balance relevance/diversity)
- Important for: broad queries, comparison questions
- Implementations: LangChain MMR search, Pinecone diversity
- Alternative: retrieve more, deduplicate, then select diverse set
- I use MMR for open-ended queries, pure similarity for specific

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How would you implement a RAG system that learns from user corrections?
diagram: [User corrects answer] -> [Store correction] -> [Update KB or fine-tune] -> [Retrieval prioritizes corrected answers]
hinglish_explanation: User corrections se RAG improve karna - jab user answer edit kare ya correct kare, wo correction store karo. Future mein same query aaye to corrected answer priority mein ho. Long-term: corrections se fine-tuning ya KB update. Active learning loop.
real_life_example: Google Maps mein user road correction submit karta hai - next users ko updated map milta hai. RAG mein same - user correction future answers improve karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Capture user corrections/edits on RAG responses
- Store as: (query, original_answer, corrected_answer, context)
- Short-term: cache corrected answers for similar queries
- Medium-term: add corrections to knowledge base
- Long-term: fine-tune model on corrections
- Priority retrieval: check corrections first
- Quality control: validate corrections (not all are right)
- I implement correction cache + quarterly KB updates

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'attention sink' in long-context LLMs?
diagram:
First few tokens get disproportionate attention regardless of content
[BOS] token acts as attention 'sink'
Implications for prompt design
hinglish_explanation: Attention sink matlab LLM first few tokens ko disproportionate attention deta hai - chahe unka content important na ho. BOS token 'attention dump' ban jaata hai. Production implication: important content start mein rakhna slightly better, system prompt high-priority tokens early.
real_life_example: Class mein teacher ke pehle 5 minutes sabse zyaada dhyan lagta hai. Attention sink same - model ke 'pehle tokens' ko attention zyaada milta hai. Prompt design mein use karo yeh knowledge.
how_to_answer:
- LLMs disproportionately attend to initial tokens
- BOS/first tokens become attention 'sinks' (absorb excess attention)
- StreamingLLM paper (Xiao et al. 2023)
- Implication: keep initial tokens stable for streaming
- For RAG: slightly favor placing critical info near start
- Window attention with attention sinks enables infinite streaming
- Different from 'lost in middle' (that's about middle positions)
- Practical: place system prompt instructions at very start

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How do you implement semantic versioning for RAG knowledge bases?
diagram:
KB v1.0 -> v1.1 (minor: add docs) -> v2.0 (major: re-embed with new model)
Track: which queries used which version, rollback capability
hinglish_explanation: RAG knowledge base ko version karo jaise software - minor (new docs add), major (embedding model change, re-index). Har response mein KB version tag karo. Rollback possible hona chahiye. A/B test new version before full deploy.
real_life_example: App ka version 2.0 release - kuch users ko old dikhao, kuch ko new. Problem aaye to rollback. RAG KB bhi same versioning deserve karta hai.
how_to_answer:
- Semantic versioning for knowledge base: major.minor.patch
- Major: embedding model change, full re-index
- Minor: new documents added, chunking unchanged
- Patch: metadata updates, typo fixes
- Tag every response with KB version used
- Enable rollback: keep previous index available
- A/B test new version before full switch
- Track quality metrics per KB version
- I maintain 2 index versions simultaneously for safe rollout

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the role of negative mining in training embedding models?
diagram:
Hard negatives: docs that are similar but NOT relevant
Training: (query, positive, hard_negative) -> model learns fine-grained differences
hinglish_explanation: Negative mining matlab training mein aise documents dhundhna jo query se similar dikhte hain but actually relevant nahi. Hard negatives se model fine-grained differences seekhta hai. Easy negatives (random docs) se model bahut nahi seekhta - hard negatives needed for good quality.
real_life_example: Cricket team selection mein close competitors (hard negatives) ke against judge karna important hai - obvious non-players (easy negatives) se compare easy hai. Embedding training mein bhi hard negatives se quality improve hoti hai.
how_to_answer:
- Hard negatives: similar-looking but irrelevant documents
- Easy negatives: random documents (too easy for model)
- Hard negatives force model to learn subtle differences
- Mining methods: BM25 top-k, in-batch, cross-batch
- Typical ratio: 1 positive : 5-15 hard negatives
- Dramatically improves embedding quality
- Tools: sentence-transformers mining utilities
- I mine hard negatives from top-50 BM25 that aren't relevant

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the concept of 'context window management' in production RAG?
diagram:
Total budget: 128k tokens
Allocate: system prompt (2k) + history (4k) + retrieved docs (8k) + response (4k)
Leave buffer for safety
hinglish_explanation: Context window management matlab available tokens ko wisely allocate karna - system prompt, history, retrieved docs, response space sab fit karna hai. Overflow se information loss hota hai. Budget planning upfront karna must hai.
real_life_example: Monthly salary budget karna - rent, food, savings, entertainment sab allocate. Context window bhi same - har component ko tokens allocate karo wisely. Overflow = trouble.
how_to_answer:
- Plan token budget across: system prompt, history, context, output
- Track actual usage per component
- Strategies: summarize history, limit retrieved chunks, trim context
- Leave 20% buffer for safety
- Dynamic: adjust context size based on query complexity
- Token counting: tiktoken for OpenAI, model-specific for others
- Overflow handling: summarize oldest history, reduce chunks
- I set hard limits: max 5 chunks, max 3 history turns

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the difference between instruction-following and chat-optimized models?
diagram:
Instruction-following: single-turn task completion (InstructGPT)
Chat-optimized: multi-turn conversation (ChatGPT, Claude)
hinglish_explanation: Instruction models single instructions follow karte hain - ek task, ek response. Chat models multi-turn conversation optimize karte hain - context maintain, personality consistent. RAG mein dono kaam karte hain - chat models better for conversational RAG.
real_life_example: Instruction = post office worker (ek kaam karo, next). Chat = personal secretary (poori conversation maintain karo, follow-ups handle karo). Chat models conversational RAG ke liye better.
how_to_answer:
- Instruction-following: optimized for single-turn task execution
- Chat-optimized: optimized for multi-turn conversations
- Chat models: better memory, personality, turn-taking
- Instruction models: better at precise task following
- Modern models (GPT-4o, Claude): good at both
- For RAG chatbot: use chat-optimized
- For batch processing: instruction-following sufficient
- API: chat completions (messages) vs completions (prompt)

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: How would you architect a RAG system for regulatory compliance (SOC2, HIPAA)?
diagram: [Encrypted storage] + [Access logs] + [Data residency] + [PII masking] + [Audit trails] + [Retention policies]
hinglish_explanation: Compliance RAG mein: data encryption (at rest + transit), access controls, audit trails, data residency (India mein data India mein), PII masking, retention policies, vendor compliance (is your LLM API provider SOC2?). Documentation bhi part of compliance.
real_life_example: Bank locker - access log, authorized persons only, CCTV, insurance. Compliance RAG same - har action logged, authorized access only, data protected, auditable.
how_to_answer:
- Encryption: at-rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.3)
- Access control: RBAC, document-level permissions
- Audit trails: immutable logs of all queries and responses
- Data residency: deploy in required geography
- PII handling: detect, mask, or redact before processing
- Vendor compliance: LLM provider SOC2/HIPAA certified?
- Retention: auto-delete after policy period
- Documentation: data flow diagrams, risk assessments
- I design compliance into architecture from day one

topic: LLM and RAG and Prompt Engineering
question: What is the future of RAG and what emerging trends should ML engineers watch?
diagram: Trends: agentic RAG, multi-modal, graph RAG, on-device RAG, self-improving RAG, real-time streaming RAG
hinglish_explanation: RAG ka future: 1) Agentic RAG (agents control retrieval) 2) Multi-modal (text+image+audio) 3) GraphRAG (knowledge graphs) 4) Edge/on-device RAG 5) Self-improving (learns from feedback) 6) Real-time streaming 7) Longer context + RAG hybrid. Field rapidly evolving hai.
real_life_example: 5 saal pehle simple keyword search tha, ab semantic RAG hai. Agle 2-3 saal mein agents + multi-modal + self-improving RAG standard ho jaayega. ML engineers ko yeh trends track karne chahiye.
how_to_answer:
- Agentic RAG: agents dynamically control retrieval decisions
- Multi-modal: text + images + audio + video retrieval
- GraphRAG: knowledge graphs + vector search combined
- Edge RAG: on-device for privacy and offline
- Self-improving: learns from user feedback continuously
- Long context + RAG hybrid: 1M context with selective retrieval
- Evaluation: better automated metrics, less human dependency
- I'm actively building with LangGraph agents + multi-modal retrieval
